title: Slay The Nightmares
subtitle: A 2.5D beat ’em up where a unicorn survives ten intense enemy waves using a horn that transforms into different weapon forms with distinct combat mechanics.
overview: Slay The Nightmares is a fast-paced 2.5D beat ’em up focused on wave-based survival. The player controls a unicorn facing escalating nightmare enemies across ten intense waves. The core hook is a transforming horn that can take multiple weapon forms, each with its own combat rhythm, attacks, and utility. The experience is built around clear readability (telegraphs, hit feedback, VFX) and a strong sense of progression as waves ramp up in difficulty.
role: I owned the full technical side of the project: engine setup and implementation of key gameplay systems including movement, combat, enemies, horn transformations, and UI logic. I prepared scenes for the 2.5D visual style by building shaders, post-processing, lighting, and weapon VFX, plus nightmare visual overlays using Shader Graph. My goal was to keep combat responsive and readable while maintaining a cohesive stylized look.
description: A 2.5D beat ’em up where a unicorn survives ten escalating waves using a transforming horn with unique weapon forms.
timelineCaptions: Early prototype: core movement, basic attacks, and first enemy prototype with a simple wave loop.
Core production: modular horn forms, enemy behaviors, UI logic, and the first full wave set with a difficulty ramp.
Polish & style: Shader Graph effects, VFX/post-process, lighting pass, readability tuning, and final balancing for 10 waves.
